No faults. 0 tasks FAILED, 0 CUDA OOM, worker exited normally with "queue empty, 8 tasks done". Queue end state verified: pending empty, done=30, 1 task (decode T=1) still running on another worker — not mine.

mcErrorMemoryValueTooLarge / "private memory" (C500 4 KB/thread cap, kernel requesting 5-7 KB/thread): 8 occurrences, ALL inside tuning blocks (verified programmatically — every MCR/mcError line falls between a "claimed"/"[cfgs]" line and the task's result line). Expected and harmless per the brief; nothing outside tuning.

Numerical note (not a fault, both sides pass the 5e-2 gate): rel_err_fused is uniformly ~2.5e-3 to 3.3e-3 across every T, roughly 7-8x the unfused error (~3-6e-4) at most sizes, and ~1000x the unfused error at T=2 where unfused is 3.3e-6. The fused error is also notably flat in T, consistent with accumulating the row sum-of-squares in the GEMM k-loop at reduced precision rather than in a dedicated fp32 pass. Worth flagging to whoever aggregates, since it is a systematic offset, not jitter.

Interpretation, respecting the ~2.2 % between-run bound: all 8 of my points have gain_spread_pct <= 1.26 %, i.e. within-task tuning was stable. The regime split is far outside noise and is real — prefill fuses profitably (1.34x at T=32768, 1.41x at T=65536, sq_redundancy=2) while every decode point I drew is a NET LOSS (0.62-0.91x, sq_redundancy=8). The 4x higher sum-of-squares redundancy in decode (8 N-tiles vs 2) tracks that loss. Within decode I do not claim a monotonic trend: the sequence 0.62, 0.65, 0.68, 0.75, 0.91, 0.76 rises then drops at T=1024, and I only hold 6 of the decode points, so the shape should be judged after merging the other two workers' rows.

No failures. Worker gpu0 exited cleanly with "[gpu0] queue empty, 11 tasks done". No task marked FAILED, no CUDA OOM, no Traceback. The only mcErrorMemoryValueTooLarge / "private memory" messages appeared inside tuning (expected C500 4 KB/thread candidate rejection) — none outside tuning. Log: /tmp/f11b_gpu0.log; JSONs: /home/zhangshuhan/fusion/results/f11b_<regime>_T<n>.json (each carries "worker": "gpu0").

Notes on the numbers (reporting only, no trend claims below the ~2.2 % resolution floor): all 11 of my points have gain_spread_pct <= 1.14 %, i.e. within-run round-to-round spread is well under the ~2.2 % between-run bound, so individual gains are stable but small differences between neighboring T are not resolved. Fusion is a win only at my two large prefill points (T=262144 gain 1.395x with sq_redundancy 2; T=8192 gain 1.188x with sq_redundancy 4). Every point with sq_redundancy 8 came out below 1.0x (0.63x-0.86x), including prefill T=512 (0.853x) and decode T=512 (0.856x), which agree with each other to ~0.4 %. rel_err_fused is consistently ~2.3e-3 to 3.1e-3, roughly 5-10x rel_err_unfused at mid/large T; at the smallest decode sizes (T=1, 4, 32) rel_err_unfused drops to ~3.2e-6 while rel_err_fused stays ~2.4e-3 to 3.1e-3 — a ~1000x gap. Both remain fp16/bf16-plausible magnitudes and the script validated every task against its fp32 reference, but the fused-side error floor sitting flat at ~3e-3 regardless of T is worth a look by whoever aggregates.
